# Limitations and Honest Scope

## This is a simulation, not flight software

* The simulator is an **educational model** of a few flight-computer
  behaviours. It has never run on a satellite, has not been tested in space,
  is not certified or qualified for flight, and has not been validated
  against any real hardware, including any Pixxel hardware.
* All telemetry is **simulated**: frames are typed or generated by scripts.
  Nothing reads a physical sensor.
* All thresholds (6.8 V, 60 °C, 15°, 10 s, 60 s, ...) are **invented
  demonstration values**. They do not come from any battery datasheet,
  thermal analysis or mission requirement.
* The requirement catalogue (`tests/requirements.json`) was written for
  this project to demonstrate traceability. It is not a real spacecraft
  requirement specification.

## Software-in-the-loop, not hardware-in-the-loop

| | This project (SIL) | Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) |
|---|---|---|
| Flight logic runs on | a desktop/CI machine | the real (or flight-like) processor |
| Sensors / radio | simulated text commands | real or emulated electrical interfaces |
| Timing | simulated clock, no real-time constraints | real-time, interrupts, jitter, watchdogs |
| Detects | logic, state-machine, validation, robustness defects | also timing, driver, electrical, integration defects |

SIL is a useful early, cheap, fast stage of verification. It does not
replace HIL testing or environmental testing (thermal vacuum, vibration,
radiation).

## Simplifications

* **No real-time behaviour:** no RTOS, scheduler, interrupts, watchdog timer
  or deadline checking. `TICK` jumps time instantly.
* **No real data links:** commands are text lines, not CCSDS packets or a
  radio protocol. There is no checksum, encryption or authentication of
  commands.
* **Simplified safety logic:** independent threshold rules with hysteresis
  only. No sensor fusion, filtering, debouncing over time, redundancy
  management, FDIR hierarchy or attitude control.
* **Single process, single thread.** No concurrency is modelled.
* **No persistence:** state lives only for the duration of one process.
* `FAULT_INJECT` is a test hook. Real flight software would not expose such
  a command.

## What the tests do and do not prove

* Passing tests show that the implementation matches **this project's
  specification** for the cases tested. They are evidence, not a proof of
  correctness.
* The test suite is extensive (boundary values, permission matrix, random
  walks, fault injection, golden regression), but **code coverage was not
  measured**, so no coverage percentage is claimed.
* The seeded-defect check shows that one specific class of bug (an off-by-one
  boundary) is detected. It does not show that every possible bug is detected.

## Environment verification status

* Built and tested on **Ubuntu 24.04 (x86_64)** with GCC 13.3 and Clang 18
  (`-Werror`), CMake 3.28, Python 3.13 and 3.11, including an AddressSanitizer
  and UBSan build.
* **macOS:** the code and scripts are written to be portable (C++17 standard
  library only, Bash 3.2-compatible scripts, `sysctl` fallback for CPU count,
  Apple Clang warning flags). They have **not yet been run on a Mac** in this
  development session. The GitHub Actions workflow includes a `macos-14` job
  to verify this automatically once it runs.
* **Jenkins:** the `Jenkinsfile` has not been executed by a real Jenkins
  server yet. Its stage commands were run in order from a clean clone. See
  [jenkins.md](jenkins.md).
* **GitHub Actions:** the workflow has not run until it is pushed to a branch
  or pull request where Actions are enabled.
